claims.text: High configurational entropy is the key factor governing the structural and chemical stability of equiatomic multimetal nanoparticles.
When the entropy of mixing dominates enthalpic tendencies for segregation and phase separation, the nanoparticles maintain a uniform single-phase solid solution.
The initial nanoparticles contain five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios and are homogeneous solid solutions.
High configurational entropy provides atomic-scale compositional uniformity.
High configurational entropy minimizes local compositional fluctuations.
High configurational entropy suppresses the formation of secondary phases.
Configurational entropy lowers the free energy of the solid-solution phase.
The entropy contribution counters enthalpic driving forces for elemental segregation.
The solid solution remains uniform when operating temperatures lie in a regime where the entropy contribution dominates.
Phase separation may occur when segregation enthalpy becomes significant or dominates entropy stabilization.
Across 473–1923 K under the stated atmospheres or thermal gradients, the nanoparticles will retain their initial single-phase structure.
Across the stated conditions, the nanoparticles will retain homogeneous chemical composition relative to the initial baseline.
Slight deliberate elemental-composition perturbations increase the enthalpic contribution or enthalpy of mixing relative to the equiatomic composition.
Compositionally perturbed nanoparticles will exhibit segregation or phase separation earlier than equiatomic nanoparticles under identical treatment.
The temperature or reactive-condition threshold for loss of entropy stabilization depends on the particular metal combination and small composition variations.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and predicted outcome assert stability across the stated 473–1923 K conditions, but the boundary limits that prediction to an undefined regime in which entropy dominates, and the uncertainty field concedes that the relevant temperature and atmosphere thresholds are unknown. Thus the stated conditions do not establish that the stability prediction should apply throughout the full range.
